Monte Carlo Uncertainty of Plasma Diagnostics

Source: R/uncertainty.R
plasma_uncertainty.Rd

Propagates the uncertainties of the line intensities, of the transition probabilities and of the electron density to the temperature of a Boltzmann or Saha-Boltzmann plot, or to the temperature and the composition of a calibration-free (CF-LIBS) analysis, by Monte Carlo simulation.

Usage

plasma_uncertainty(
  object,
  n = 1000,
  level = 0.95,
  aki_rsd = NULL,
  electron_density_se = 0,
  temperature_se = 0
)

Arguments

object

A fit returned by boltzmann(), saha_boltzmann() or cf_libs().

n

The number of draws. Default is 1000.

level

The confidence level of the intervals. Default is 0.95.

aki_rsd

The relative standard uncertainties of the transition probabilities, such as 0.1 for 10%: one value, or one per line. By default, they are taken from the column accuracy of the lines.

electron_density_se

The standard uncertainty of the electron density of the fit, in cm\(^{-3}\). Default is 0.

temperature_se

For a cf_libs() fit given the temperature: the standard uncertainty of the temperature, in K. Default is 0.

Value

An object of class specproc_uncertainty, a list with

  • estimates: a tibble with one row per quantity: the quantity ("temperature", "atomic_fraction" or "mass_fraction"), the element (CF-LIBS), the estimate of the fit, the standard uncertainty se (the standard deviation of the draws), and the lower and upper bounds of the interval;

  • draws: a tibble of the draws, with the draw number, the temperature and, for CF-LIBS, the element, atomic_fraction and mass_fraction;

  • inputs: a tibble with the relative standard uncertainties of the intensity (intensity_rsd) and of the transition probability (aki_rsd) of each line;

  • electron_density_rsd and temperature_rsd: the relative standard uncertainties of the electron density and of a given temperature (NULL when not used by the fit);

  • chi_squared: the reduced chi-squared of the fit (NA when the temperature is given, or when a point has no stated uncertainty);

  • temperature_se: the standard error of the temperature of the fit;

  • n, level, the number of failed draws and the method.

Details

Each of the n draws perturbs the inputs of the fit within their uncertainties and repeats the fit. The standard deviation of the results is their standard uncertainty, and their quantiles give the interval at level. The perturbations are lognormal (multiplicative), with the relative standard uncertainties of the inputs, so that intensities, transition probabilities and densities stay positive. The sources are:

  • the intensities: the column intensity_se of the lines (standard errors, in the units of intensity), as returned by line_intensities();

  • the transition probabilities: aki_rsd, or else the accuracy grades of the NIST Atomic Spectra Database in the column accuracy (see aki_uncertainty());

  • the electron density, for Saha-Boltzmann plots and CF-LIBS: electron_density_se, for example from electron_density_uncertainty();

  • the temperature, for a cf_libs() fit given the temperature: temperature_se.

A source that is not given is taken as exact. The errors of different lines are taken as independent, and the partition functions and the ionization energies as exact. Lines corrected by correct_self_absorption() are not independent: their corrected intensities are computed from their reference line.

The interval reflects the stated uncertainties of the inputs, whereas the standard error of the fit (temperature_se of the fit) reflects the scatter of the points about the fitted line. The reduced chi-squared compares the two: \(\chi^2_\nu = \sum_i (r_i / \sigma_i)^2 / \nu\), where \(r_i\) are the residuals of the fit, \(\sigma_i\) the standard uncertainties of the ordinates of the points (from those of the intensities and of the transition probabilities) and \(\nu\) the residual degrees of freedom. Near 1, the stated uncertainties explain the scatter. Well above 1, other errors scatter the points (self-absorption, spectral response, departures from LTE, or understated uncertainties) and the interval is too narrow. Well below 1, the uncertainties are overstated; the NIST grades are upper bounds.

A draw whose Boltzmann plot has a non-negative slope has no finite temperature: it counts as an infinite temperature in the interval, whose upper bound can then be infinite, and is left out of the standard deviation. A CF-LIBS draw that fails is left out, with a warning.

Use set.seed() for reproducible results.

References

  • JCGM 101:2008. Evaluation of measurement data - Supplement 1 to the "Guide to the expression of uncertainty in measurement" - Propagation of distributions using a Monte Carlo method. Joint Committee for Guides in Metrology.

See also

aki_uncertainty(), electron_density_uncertainty(), boltzmann(), saha_boltzmann(), cf_libs(), line_intensities()

Author

Christian L. Goueguel

Examples

data(forageLIBS)
mean_spectrum <- colMeans(forageLIBS[-(1:14)])
# calcium lines, with their atomic data and accuracy grades from the NIST
# database
atomic <- data.frame(
  species = c(rep("Ca I", 6), rep("Ca II", 4)),
  stage = c(rep(1, 6), rep(2, 4)),
  wavelength = c(428.301, 430.253, 431.865, 445.478, 612.222, 616.217,
                 315.887, 317.933, 370.603, 373.690),
  Aki = c(4.34e7, 1.36e8, 7.40e7, 8.70e7, 2.87e7, 4.77e7, 3.10e8, 3.60e8, 8.80e7, 1.70e8),
  accuracy = c("C+", "C+", "C+", "C", "C", "C", "C", "C", "C", "C"),
  gk = c(5, 5, 3, 7, 3, 3, 4, 6, 2, 2),
  Ek = c(4.780, 4.780, 4.769, 4.681, 3.910, 3.910, 7.047, 7.050, 6.468, 6.468)
)
lines <- line_intensities(mean_spectrum, atomic, baseline = TRUE)
fit <- saha_boltzmann(lines, ionization_energy = 6.113, electron_density = 1.9e17)

# with a 15% standard uncertainty of the electron density
set.seed(1)
u <- plasma_uncertainty(fit, electron_density_se = 0.15 * 1.9e17)
u
#> Monte Carlo uncertainty of a Saha-Boltzmann plot
#> 1000 draws, 95% intervals
#> 
#> Intensities:              0.39% to 4.5%
#> Transition probabilities: 18% to 25%
#> Electron density:         15%
#> Reduced chi-squared:      1.53
#> 
#>  quantity    estimate se  lower upper
#>  temperature 8092     124 7862  8353 
#> 
#> Standard error of the fit (scatter of the points): 124 K
u$estimates
#> # A tibble: 1 × 6
#>   quantity    element estimate    se lower upper
#>   <chr>       <chr>      <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1 temperature NA         8092.  124. 7862. 8353.
